name: Tax Refund and Identity-Based Benefit Fraud
description: Offenders file false returns or benefit claims using stolen or fabricated identities and direct refunds to accounts they control. Banks see inbound refunds to unrelated accounts and mule behaviour.

sources.text: IRS and HMRC public guidance on refund and identity fraud (general)
UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (specify year, e.g. 2025)

exposure.rationale: Refunds/benefit payments landing in mule or prepaid accounts.

indicators.name: Refund or benefit credited to account of different name
indicators.canon: Payment directed to personal or third-party account
indicators.desc: Payment is requested to, or credited to, a personal, third-party or differently named account rather than the contracted payee.
indicators.ctx: Payee name does not match the recipient listed.
refs: IRS and HMRC public guidance on refund and identity fraud (general)

indicators.name: Multiple refunds into the same account
indicators.canon: Multiple refunds into the same account
indicators.desc: Unrelated refunds converge on one account or card.
indicators.ctx: Unrelated refunds converge on one account or card.
refs: IRS and HMRC public guidance on refund and identity fraud (general)

indicators.name: Account holder surprised by refund or victim reports unexpected claim
indicators.canon: Account holder surprised by refund or victim reports unexpected claim
indicators.desc: customer discovers a fraudulent return in their name.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: customer discovers a fraudulent return in their name.
refs: IRS and HMRC public guidance on refund and identity fraud (general)

indicators.name: Recently opened account receiving government payments
indicators.canon: Recently opened account receiving government payments
indicators.desc: New accounts used to receive claims.
indicators.ctx: New accounts used to receive claims.
refs: IRS and HMRC public guidance on refund and identity fraud (general)

indicators.name: Rapid withdrawals or transfers after refund
indicators.canon: Large credit followed by prompt withdrawals
indicators.desc: A cheque deposit or refund is credited and quickly withdrawn or transferred before it clears or is verified.
refs: IRS and HMRC public guidance on refund and identity fraud (general)

indicators.name: Application data shared across many claimants
indicators.canon: Shared device, contact or address data across many applicants or senders
indicators.desc: The same device fingerprint, IP, phone, email or address appears across many applications, claims or apparent customers.
indicators.ctx: Same device, IP or address in many claims.
refs: IRS and HMRC public guidance on refund and identity fraud (general)

indicators.name: Prepaid cards loaded with refunds
refs: IRS and HMRC public guidance on refund and identity fraud (general)

indicators.name: Income or dependants inconsistent with profile
indicators.canon: Claim details inconsistent with income, residency or account history
indicators.desc: Declared income, dependants or circumstances conflict with data held on the customer.
indicators.ctx: Claim data diverges from account history.
refs: IRS and HMRC public guidance on refund and identity fraud (general)
